plan: sibling definition, label-free sibling detector, and expected benefit from output agreement
status: exploratory (EyePACS confirmation set and DDR previously opened); to be repeated on the dermatology arm
definition: A sibling is a model that starts from the same pretrained checkpoint (same architecture and same starting weights), whatever its seed, output format (binary or 5-class), fine-tuning variant or training recipe.
part_A_checkpoint_rule: Rerun the enriched-calibration simulation (k severe plus k controls, k = 25, 50, 100, 200; 200 draws) with eligibility defined by the checkpoint rule instead of the architecture-family rule; rules: enriched AUC, random, true strongest, oracle; sites EyePACS (22-model zoo, all distinct checkpoints) and DDR (11 paper architectures).

part_B_detector.pool_EyePACS: confirmation set: 33 paper models (11 variants x 3 seeds), 6 starting-weights models (ViT-B MAE and DINOv2, ResNet50 SWSL and DINO, 3 seeds each), and the 22 full-recipe zoo models (different seed and recipe from the paper models sharing their checkpoints)
part_B_detector.pair_labels: sibling (same checkpoint id) vs non-sibling; sibling subtypes: seed only, output format, fine-tuning variant (RETFound family), recipe (zoo vs paper model)
label_free_agreement: Spearman rank correlation of scores on all images
Cohen's kappa of refer/not-refer decisions at the site referral fraction
analyses: AUC for separating siblings from non-siblings
threshold chosen on EyePACS (Youden) and applied unchanged to DDR (sensitivity, specificity)

part_C_expected_benefit: For every ordered non-identical pair, share of the deployed model's severe misses rescued at matched referral volume, plotted and regressed against label-free kappa; reported with and without the deployed model's own miss count as a covariate; fitted on EyePACS and checked on DDR
what_counts_as_useful: sibling vs non-sibling AUC of 0.9 or more with a threshold that transfers to DDR; and a monotone relationship between label-free agreement and expected severe rescue that holds at both sites
